Definition: to bear young; causatively, to beget; medically, to act as midwife; specifically, to show lineage
BiblicalUsage: Yâlad is the word for bearing and begetting, the verb that carries the genealogies of Scripture from Adam to Seth and on through every generation. Abraham called his son Isaac, the child Sarah bare to him in old age, and Hannah bare Samuel because she had asked him of the LORD. The word reaches its height when the LORD says to His Son, this day have I begotten thee, so that birth itself becomes the language of God's own promise.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe every birth in Scripture is God's doing, from the first son of Adam to the child of a barren woman. My position is that God keeps His promises through generations, one birth at a time, and the line that began with Adam ends with Christ. And I hold that being begotten of God is not a figure for me but the new birth by which I belong to Him.
